name: device_js_evidence_surface

ownership.argument: How the QuickJS heap and the qjs builtin behave on a Mirage p67 device, recorded because the JS object layout evidence has to be taken at runtime: the heap is in PSRAM at 0x3C000000, not in the 0x20000000 RAM, so a snapshot of RAM alone shows nothing. A staged script run as `qjs /data/<name>.js &` with a tight `do{}while(1)` keeps the heap alive and does starve NSH (miragectl sh then times out) without blocking QMP memory reads.

provenance.source: Device probe on Mirage `probe-p67` (3.101.043): `var ab = new ArrayBuffer(512)` filled with 0xA7 was found as a 512-byte run at 0x3C39E750, and `new Uint8Array(8)` filled with 0xB3 as an 8-byte run at 0x3C27A380, both inside a snapshot of 0x3C000000+4 MiB taken with QMP `xp` while the script was alive. The same RAM snapshot at 0x20000000..0x20160000 contained neither marker. qjs on this build has no `print`; `console.log` works and `throw <expr>` surfaces a value in the interpreter error text.

notes: Evidence-surface note for the JS object question, not an address. The class-id hop (data pointer -> JSArrayBuffer -> JSObject.u.array_buffer -> class id at object+6) was not completed in that session, and no pointer to the flash name blob exists at runtime either, so the descriptor-name route does not work on this build.
